history: Autódromo Internacional de Tarumã, located near Viamão in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, has been a cornerstone of Brazilian motorsport since its inauguration in 1970. The circuit, designed by Orlando Menegaz, was built to replace the street circuits that previously hosted races in the region. Throughout its history, Tarumã has hosted numerous national championships, including Stock Car Brasil, Formula Truck, and Brazilian Formula Three. The Internacional layout, its primary configuration, has been the stage for countless thrilling races, showcasing the skills of Brazil's top drivers. The track has undergone several renovations over the years to improve safety and maintain its relevance in modern motorsport.
atmosphere: The roar of engines echoes across the grassy plains surrounding Tarumã as a Stock Car Brasil race unfolds on the Internacional layout. The air is thick with anticipation, mixed with the smell of burning rubber and high-octane fuel. The grandstands are packed with passionate fans, waving flags and cheering on their favorite drivers. The energy is palpable, a blend of excitement and nervous tension as the cars navigate the fast, flowing corners. The sun beats down relentlessly, adding to the intensity of the event, while the sounds of samba music drift from nearby vendors, creating a uniquely Brazilian racing atmosphere.
trackCharacter: The Internacional layout at Tarumã is a fast and flowing circuit that rewards bravery and precision. Its blend of high-speed corners and short straights demands a car with excellent aerodynamic balance and strong engine performance. Drivers need to be committed through the fast Esses and have the courage to carry maximum speed through the Curva do Tala Larga to set a quick lap time. Unlike some more technical circuits, Tarumã is all about maintaining momentum and minimizing compromises, rewarding a driver who can string together a series of near-perfect corners.

famousCorners.name: Curva 1
famousCorners.description: The first corner is a fast right-hander taken at high speed, requiring commitment and precise placement.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining momentum and carrying enough speed without running wide.

famousCorners.name: Curva 2 (Curva da Ferradura)
famousCorners.description: A long, sweeping right-hand corner that tests a car's balance and the driver's nerve.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining a tight line and managing tire wear throughout the corner.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Tala Larga
famousCorners.description: A quick right-hand kink that requires bravery and a good car balance.
famousCorners.challenge: Carrying as much speed as possible while avoiding understeer or oversteer.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Laço
famousCorners.description: A slower left-hand hairpin that is one of the tightest turns on the circuit.
famousCorners.challenge: Braking late and accurately, while setting up for a good exit.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Super Gaúcho
famousCorners.description: A fast right-hander that leads onto the main straight.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining exit speed to maximize acceleration down the straight.

keyFactors: Tire management, especially on the right-hand side
Consistent corner exits to maximize speed on the short straights
overtakingSpots: Into Curva 1 (especially on the opening lap)
Down the main straight, using the slipstream

weatherNotes: The weather at Tarumã can be unpredictable, with hot and humid conditions common during the summer months. Rain showers can also occur, making track conditions tricky and adding an extra element of strategy to races. The open nature of the surrounding landscape can also lead to strong winds, which can affect car handling, especially in the high-speed corners.
drivingAdvice: To be fast at Tarumã on the Internacional layout, you need to be aggressive and confident. Carry as much speed as possible through the Esses, trusting your car's grip and balance. Curva do Tala Larga is a key corner where you can gain or lose significant time. Be precise with your braking into Curva do Laço, and focus on getting a good exit to maximize your speed down the following straight. Tire management is crucial, especially on the right-hand side, so avoid overdriving the car early in the race.
famousRaces: Stock Car Brasil races at Tarumã are always action-packed, with close battles and dramatic finishes.
Brazilian Formula Three races have showcased the talents of up-and-coming drivers.
Formula Truck events at Tarumã have drawn large crowds, eager to see the spectacle of these powerful machines.
localCulture: The region surrounding Tarumã is rich in Gaucho culture, with strong traditions of cattle ranching, music, and dance. Local cuisine features hearty dishes such as churrasco (barbecue) and chimarrão (mate tea). Paddock life at Tarumã is friendly and welcoming, with teams and drivers often sharing stories and experiences. The local fans are passionate and knowledgeable, creating a vibrant and supportive atmosphere.
